Action.doc: Action is what happens to dependent rows when their parent is deleted or its key changes.

Add.decl: func Add[T any](h Handle, entity *T) error
Add.doc: Add schedules a new entity for insertion by the next SaveChanges.

Added.doc: Added entities are inserted by the next SaveChanges.

AfterDeleter.doc: AfterDeleter runs after an entity is deleted.

AfterIncluder.doc: AfterIncluder runs on each entity a query returns, after Include, so its relations are there.

AfterInserter.doc: AfterInserter runs after an entity is inserted.

AfterLoader.doc: AfterLoader runs on each entity a query returns, before Include.

AfterUpdater.doc: AfterUpdater runs after an entity is updated.

Alert.doc: Alert is a warning about how the database is being used.

AllOf.decl: func AllOf[V comparable](v V, fields ...*V) Cond
AllOf.doc: AllOf matches rows where every one of fields equals v.

And.doc: And matches rows where every condition matches.

AnyOf.decl: func AnyOf[V comparable](v V, fields ...*V) Cond
AnyOf.doc: AnyOf matches rows where at least one of fields equals v.

Assignment.doc: Assignment sets a column in a bulk update.

Attach.decl: func Attach[T any](h Handle, entity *T) error
Attach.doc: Attach tracks an entity as it is, assuming it matches the database.

Attempts.doc: Attempts retries a transaction that fails from a deadlock or serialization conflict, up to n runs in all, waiting a little longer each time.

AvgOf.decl: func AvgOf[T any, V Number](ctx context.Context, q *Query[T], field *V) (float64, error)
AvgOf.doc: AvgOf averages a column over matching rows, giving zero if there are none.

AvgRelated.decl: func AvgRelated[R any, V Number](rel *[]R, field *V, conds ...Cond) Expr[sql.Null[float64]]
AvgRelated.doc: AvgRelated averages a field of the related rows.

Base.doc: Base is an optional embeddable model base.

BatchSize.doc: BatchSize sets the most rows in one statement.

BeforeDeleter.doc: BeforeDeleter runs before an entity is deleted.

BeforeInserter.doc: BeforeInserter runs before an entity is inserted.

BeforeUpdater.doc: BeforeUpdater runs before a changed entity is updated.

Begin.decl: func Begin[DB any](ctx context.Context, db *DB, options ...TxOption) (*DB, error)
Begin.doc: Begin starts a transaction and returns a context bound to it.

Between.decl: func Between[V Ordered](field *V, low, high V) Cond
Between.doc: Between matches rows where field is within low and high, inclusive.

BulkRows.doc: BulkRows is entities prepared for a bulk loader outside ant, such as COPY.

CaseExpr.Else.doc: Else finishes the expression with a value for when no branch matches.

CaseExpr.ElseExpr.doc: ElseExpr finishes the expression, with an expression for rows no branch matched.

CaseExpr.End.doc: End finishes the expression, which is NULL when no branch matches.

CaseExpr.When.decl: func (c CaseExpr[V]) When(cond Cond, then V) CaseExpr[V]

CaseExpr.WhenExpr.decl: func (c CaseExpr[V]) WhenExpr(cond Cond, then Expr[V]) CaseExpr[V]
CaseExpr.WhenExpr.doc: WhenExpr adds a branch whose result is an expression, such as another column.

Change.doc: Change describes one entity a SaveChanges is about to write.

Clone.doc: Clone returns a copy of entity with its key and relations cleared, ready to be inserted as a new row.

Coalesce.doc: Coalesce returns the first non-NULL of field and fallback.

Col.doc: Col returns the expression for a column.

Collate.doc: Collate applies a collation to a text column.

ColumnBuilder.doc: ColumnBuilder configures how a column is declared in migrations.

ColumnBuilder.Comment.doc: Comment describes the column in the database.

ColumnBuilder.Default.doc: Default sets the column's default, a SQL expression such as now() or 'draft'.

ColumnBuilder.Enum.doc: Enum stores the column as a native enum type, which migrations create and extend.

ColumnBuilder.Fixed.doc: Fixed makes a string column exactly n characters.

ColumnBuilder.Generated.doc: Generated makes the column a stored generated column, computed by the database from expr.

ColumnBuilder.Length.doc: Length limits a string column to n characters.

ColumnBuilder.NotNull.doc: NotNull refuses NULL in a column whose Go type could hold it.

ColumnBuilder.Nullable.doc: Nullable allows NULL in a column whose Go type has no way to hold it.

ColumnBuilder.Precision.doc: Precision makes the column an exact number with the given digits in total and after the point.

ColumnBuilder.Sensitive.doc: Sensitive keeps the column's values out of logs, even with LogValues.

ColumnBuilder.Sequence.doc: Sequence fills the column from a database sequence, which migrations create.

ColumnBuilder.Type.doc: Type sets the database type, written as it would be in SQL.

ColumnBuilder.Unique.doc: Unique adds a unique constraint on the column, like the ant:"unique" tag.

ConcurrencyError.doc: ConcurrencyError is the ErrConcurrency from SaveChanges, naming the row.

Conflict.doc: Conflict says what to do when an insert hits a unique constraint.

Conflict.And.doc: And adds a column for a constraint on several columns.

Conflict.DoUpdate.doc: DoUpdate overwrites only the named columns of the existing row.

Conflict.Set.doc: Set assigns values on conflict, as well as any named in DoUpdate.

Context.doc: Context is embedded in a user's database struct.

Context.ClearTracked.doc: ClearTracked stops tracking everything, forgetting unsaved changes.

Context.Close.doc: Close closes the underlying connection pool, for every context that shares it.

Context.Commit.doc: Commit ends a transaction from Begin, keeping its changes.

Context.DB.doc: DB returns the underlying pool, for settings such as SetMaxOpenConns.

Context.DebugTracked.doc: DebugTracked describes every tracked entity, for logs and debugging.

Context.Dialect.doc: Dialect returns the dialect the context was opened with.

Context.EnsureCreated.doc: EnsureCreated creates the tables, indexes, and foreign keys of models that have no table yet, directly from the structs, and leaves existing tables as they are.

Context.EnsureDeleted.doc: EnsureDeleted drops the tables of the context's models, with their data and whatever depends on them.

Context.HasChanges.doc: HasChanges reports whether SaveChanges has anything to write.

Context.Release.decl: func (c *Context) Release(ctx context.Context, name string) error
Context.Release.doc: Release forgets a savepoint, keeping its changes.

Context.Rollback.doc: Rollback ends a transaction from Begin, discarding its changes.

Context.RollbackTo.decl: func (c *Context) RollbackTo(ctx context.Context, name string) error
Context.RollbackTo.doc: RollbackTo undoes the statements since a savepoint.

Context.SaveChanges.doc: SaveChanges writes every change to tracked entities in one transaction: inserts and updates with parents first, then deletes with children first.

Context.Savepoint.decl: func (c *Context) Savepoint(ctx context.Context, name string) error
Context.Savepoint.doc: Savepoint marks a point to return to with RollbackTo.

Context.Tx.decl: func (c *Context) Tx[DB any](ctx context.Context, f func(tx *DB) error, options ...TxOption) error
Context.Tx.doc: Tx runs f in a transaction, passing a context of the same type bound to it.

CountDistinct.doc: CountDistinct counts the different non-NULL values of field.

CountOf.doc: CountOf counts rows where field is not NULL.

CountRelated.doc: CountRelated counts the rows related through a one-to-many relation that meet conds.

CurrentTx.doc: CurrentTx returns the transaction a context is bound to, or nil.

CursorPage.doc: CursorPage is one page from After.

CursorPage.Next.doc: Next is the cursor for the following page, empty on the last page.

DatePart.doc: DatePart extracts part of a date column, such as "year" or "month".

Dec.decl: func Dec[V Number](field *V, n V) Assignment
Dec.doc: Dec subtracts n from a numeric column, in the database.

Deleted.doc: Deleted entities are removed by the next SaveChanges.

DeletedAt.doc: DeletedAt is the type of a soft delete field.

DenseRank.doc: DenseRank ranks rows within a window, with no gaps after ties.

Diagnostics.doc: Diagnostics configures warnings about query patterns.

Diagnostics.Budget.doc: Budget alerts when statements in a scope spend longer than this in total, which a slow-query log cannot see if each one is fast.

Diagnostics.RepeatLimit.doc: RepeatLimit alerts when one statement runs more than this many times in a scope, which is what an N+1 pattern looks like.

DryRun.decl: func DryRun[DB any](ctx context.Context, db *DB, fn func(tx *DB) error) ([]Statement, error)
DryRun.doc: DryRun runs fn in a transaction and rolls it back, returning every statement it ran.

Entity.doc: Entity is implemented by models that override conventions.

EntityEntry.doc: EntityEntry inspects one entity's tracking state.

EntityEntry.Changed.doc: Changed returns the names of the fields that differ from what was loaded.

EntityEntry.State.doc: State returns the entity's state, comparing it with what was loaded.

Entry.doc: Entry returns the tracking state of an entity.

Eq.decl: func Eq[V comparable](field *V, v V) Cond
Eq.doc: Eq matches rows where field equals v.

EqCol.doc: EqCol matches rows where two columns are equal.

ErrBadSchema.doc: ErrBadSchema reports models that cannot become a valid schema.

ErrConcurrency.decl: var ErrConcurrency = errors.New("ant: row was changed or removed since it was loaded")
ErrConcurrency.doc: ErrConcurrency reports that SaveChanges found a row changed or removed since it was loaded.

ErrCursor.doc: ErrCursor reports a cursor that this query cannot use.

ErrCycle.decl: var ErrCycle = errors.New("ant: new entities depend on each other")
ErrCycle.doc: ErrCycle reports new entities that depend on each other, so neither can be inserted first.

ErrIncludeInEach.decl: var ErrIncludeInEach = errors.New("ant: Each does not support Include")
ErrIncludeInEach.doc: ErrIncludeInEach reports Include with Each, which would need a second query while rows stream.

ErrIncludeInSubquery.decl: var ErrIncludeInSubquery = errors.New("ant: subquery cannot use Include")
ErrIncludeInSubquery.doc: ErrIncludeInSubquery reports a query with Include used as a subquery.

ErrKeyChanged.decl: var ErrKeyChanged = errors.New("ant: primary key of a tracked entity was changed")
ErrKeyChanged.doc: ErrKeyChanged reports a tracked entity whose primary key was modified.

ErrKeyType.decl: var ErrKeyType = errors.New("ant: key type does not match the primary key")
ErrKeyType.doc: ErrKeyType reports a key whose type does not match the primary key.

ErrMultipleRows.decl: var ErrMultipleRows = errors.New("ant: query matched more than one row")
ErrMultipleRows.doc: ErrMultipleRows reports that Single matched more than one row.

ErrNilEntity.decl: var ErrNilEntity = errors.New("ant: entity is nil")
ErrNilEntity.doc: ErrNilEntity reports a nil pointer passed to a write.

ErrNoAssignment.decl: var ErrNoAssignment = errors.New("ant: update has no assignments")
ErrNoAssignment.doc: ErrNoAssignment reports an Update with nothing to set.

ErrNoColumnType.decl: var ErrNoColumnType = errors.New("ant: no database type for field")
ErrNoColumnType.doc: ErrNoColumnType reports a field whose database type cannot be worked out from its Go type.

ErrNoColumns.decl: var ErrNoColumns = errors.New("ant: query selects no columns")
ErrNoColumns.doc: ErrNoColumns reports a query whose selection leaves no columns.

ErrNoCondition.decl: var ErrNoCondition = errors.New("ant: bulk write has no condition")
ErrNoCondition.doc: ErrNoCondition reports a bulk write with no condition.

ErrNoContext.decl: var ErrNoContext = errors.New("ant: type does not embed ant.Context")
ErrNoContext.doc: ErrNoContext reports a type passed to Open that does not embed Context.

ErrNoForeignKey.doc: ErrNoForeignKey reports a relation whose foreign key cannot be found by convention.

ErrNoKey.decl: var ErrNoKey = errors.New("ant: model has no primary key")
ErrNoKey.doc: ErrNoKey reports a key operation on a model with no primary key.

ErrNoRows.decl: var ErrNoRows = errors.New("ant: no rows given")
ErrNoRows.doc: ErrNoRows reports an operation given no rows to work on.

ErrNotColumn.decl: var ErrNotColumn = errors.New("ant: field is a relation, not a column")
ErrNotColumn.doc: ErrNotColumn reports a probe field that is a relation, used as a column.

ErrNotFound.doc: ErrNotFound reports that a query for one row matched none.

ErrNotImplemented.doc: ErrNotImplemented reports a feature with no implementation yet.

ErrNotInTx.decl: var ErrNotInTx = errors.New("ant: not in a transaction")
ErrNotInTx.doc: ErrNotInTx reports Commit, Rollback, or a savepoint outside a transaction.

ErrNotManyToMany.decl: var ErrNotManyToMany = errors.New("ant: relation is not many-to-many")
ErrNotManyToMany.doc: ErrNotManyToMany reports a link operation on another kind of relation.

ErrNotOpen.decl: var ErrNotOpen = errors.New("ant: context is not open")
ErrNotOpen.doc: ErrNotOpen reports a table or context that did not come from Open.

ErrNotProbe.decl: var ErrNotProbe = errors.New("ant: pointer is not a field of a probe from ant.Fields")
ErrNotProbe.doc: ErrNotProbe reports a field pointer that does not come from Fields.

ErrNotRelation.decl: var ErrNotRelation = errors.New("ant: field is not a relation")
ErrNotRelation.doc: ErrNotRelation reports a probe field that is not a relation.

ErrNotSoftDeleted.decl: var ErrNotSoftDeleted = errors.New("ant: model has no DeletedAt field")
ErrNotSoftDeleted.doc: ErrNotSoftDeleted reports Restore on a model with no DeletedAt field.

ErrNotTracked.decl: var ErrNotTracked = errors.New("ant: entity is not tracked")
ErrNotTracked.doc: ErrNotTracked reports an operation on an entity the context is not tracking.

ErrReadOnly.decl: var ErrReadOnly = errors.New("ant: model is read-only")
ErrReadOnly.doc: ErrReadOnly reports a write to a read-only model, such as a view.

ErrThenWithoutOrder.decl: var ErrThenWithoutOrder = errors.New("ant: ThenBy needs a preceding OrderBy")
ErrThenWithoutOrder.doc: ErrThenWithoutOrder reports ThenBy on a query with no OrderBy.

ErrTxDone.decl: var ErrTxDone = errors.New("ant: transaction has ended")
ErrTxDone.doc: ErrTxDone reports use of a transaction after it ended.

ErrTxType.decl: var ErrTxType = errors.New("ant: Tx closure takes a different context type")
ErrTxType.doc: ErrTxType reports a Tx closure whose parameter is not this context's type.

ErrUnknownColumn.decl: var ErrUnknownColumn = errors.New("ant: result column has no field")
ErrUnknownColumn.doc: ErrUnknownColumn reports a result column with no field, under WithStrict.

ErrUnsupported.doc: ErrUnsupported reports something the connected database cannot do, such as MERGE on MySQL.

ErrWrongModel.decl: var ErrWrongModel = errors.New("ant: field belongs to a model outside this query")
ErrWrongModel.doc: ErrWrongModel reports a probe from a model the query does not use.

Events.doc: Events are callbacks on a context's unit of work.

Events.Saved.doc: Saved runs after SaveChanges commits, or, in a transaction, after it wrote.

Events.StateChanged.decl: StateChanged func(model string, entity any, from, to State)
Events.StateChanged.doc: StateChanged runs when an entity is marked with a new state, such as by Remove.

Events.Tracked.doc: Tracked runs when the tracker starts following an entity.

Exists.doc: Exists matches rows for which q returns anything.

Expr.doc: Expr is a typed SQL expression: a column, an aggregate, or a raw fragment.

Expr.Asc.doc: Asc orders by the expression, ascending.

Expr.Desc.doc: Desc orders by the expression, descending.

Expr.Eq.doc: Eq matches rows where the expression equals v.

Expr.EqExpr.doc: EqExpr matches rows where two expressions are equal.

Expr.Filter.doc: Filter limits an aggregate to rows that meet conds.

Expr.Gt.doc: Gt matches rows where the expression is greater than v.

Expr.GtExpr.doc: GtExpr matches rows where the expression is greater than another expression.

Expr.Gte.doc: Gte matches rows where the expression is greater than or equal to v.

Expr.IsNotNull.doc: IsNotNull matches rows where the expression is not NULL.

Expr.IsNull.doc: IsNull matches rows where the expression is NULL.

Expr.Lt.doc: Lt matches rows where the expression is less than v.

Expr.LtExpr.doc: LtExpr matches rows where the expression is less than another expression.

Expr.Lte.doc: Lte matches rows where the expression is less than or equal to v.

Expr.Ne.doc: Ne matches rows where the expression does not equal v.

Expr.Over.doc: Over makes an aggregate or ranking function a window function.

F.doc: F names a column, for APIs that take a list of columns of different types.

FailedCond.doc: FailedCond returns a condition that reports err at the terminal call, for use by condition helpers that can fail.

FailedExpr.doc: FailedExpr returns an expression that reports err at the terminal call, for helpers that can fail while building one.

FailedSQL.doc: FailedSQL returns the statement behind a query error, or "".

FieldConvention.doc: FieldConvention is one column, offered to a rule from WithConvention.

FieldConvention.SetLength.doc: SetLength limits a string column, as ColumnBuilder.Length does.

FieldConvention.SetSensitive.doc: SetSensitive keeps the column out of logs, as ColumnBuilder.Sensitive does.

FieldConvention.SetType.doc: SetType sets the database type, as ColumnBuilder.Type does.

FieldRef.doc: FieldRef names a column of any type, from F.

Fields.doc: Fields returns a probe for T. A probe holds no data.

ForeignKeyBuilder.doc: ForeignKeyBuilder configures a foreign key from ModelBuilder.ForeignKey.

ForeignKeyBuilder.Name.doc: Name names the constraint, in place of table_columns_fkey.

ForeignKeyBuilder.NoIndex.doc: NoIndex leaves out the index migrations otherwise add on the columns.

ForeignKeyBuilder.OnDelete.doc: OnDelete sets the action when the parent is deleted.

ForeignKeyBuilder.OnUpdate.doc: OnUpdate sets the action when the parent's key changes.

ForeignKeyBuilder.References.doc: References names the columns the key points to, in order.

FromFunc.decl: func FromFunc[T any](h Handle, call string, args ...any) *Query[T]
FromFunc.doc: FromFunc reads from a table-valued function, written with ? for its arguments, as in generate_series(?, ?).

FromRaw.decl: func FromRaw[T any](h Handle, text string, args ...any) *Query[T]
FromRaw.doc: FromRaw returns a query over raw SQL, which conditions, ordering, and paging then build on.

Func.decl: func Func[R any](name string, args ...any) Expr[R]
Func.doc: Func calls a database function by name.

Future.doc: Future matches rows where a time column is after the database's current time.

GenerateKey.decl: func GenerateKey[E, V any](b *ModelBuilder[E], field *V, fn func() V)
GenerateKey.doc: GenerateKey sets a primary key that fn fills in Go when it is zero, such as a UUID.

Gob.doc: Gob stores a Go value in a binary column with encoding/gob, for a value that only Go reads and JSON does not fit.

GraphNode.doc: GraphNode is one entity TrackGraph reached.

GraphNode.HasKey.doc: HasKey reports whether the entity has a key already, which usually means the row exists.

GraphNode.Parent.doc: a pointer to the entity it was reached from, or nil

Grouped.doc: Grouped is a query with GROUP BY.

Grouped.Having.doc: Having keeps groups that meet conds, which can use aggregates such as ant.Count().Gt(1).

Grouped.Limit.doc: Limit caps the number of groups returned.

Grouped.Order.doc: Order orders the groups by terms from Asc and Desc.

Gt.decl: func Gt[V Ordered](field *V, v V) Cond
Gt.doc: Gt matches rows where field is greater than v.

Gte.decl: func Gte[V Ordered](field *V, v V) Cond
Gte.doc: Gte matches rows where field is greater than or equal to v.

Handle.doc: Handle is any value that embeds Context, such as a *AppDB.

Has.doc: Has matches rows with at least one related row in a one-to-many relation that meets conds.

HasNone.doc: HasNone matches rows with no related row that meets conds.

HasOne.doc: HasOne matches rows with a related row in a many-to-one or one-to-one relation that meets conds.

In.doc: In matches rows where field equals one of values.

InSub.decl: func InSub[V any](field *V, sub Sub[V]) Cond
InSub.doc: InSub matches rows where field is one of the subquery's values.

InTuples.doc: InTuples matches rows whose columns, taken together, equal one of the tuples:

Inc.decl: func Inc[V Number](field *V, n V) Assignment
Inc.doc: Inc adds n to a numeric column, in the database.

IndexBuilder.And.doc: And adds a column to the index.

IndexBuilder.AndExpr.doc: AndExpr adds a SQL expression to the index.

IndexBuilder.Concurrently.doc: Concurrently builds the index without blocking writes, when it is added to a table that already exists.

IndexBuilder.Desc.doc: Desc sorts the most recently added column in descending order.

IndexBuilder.Include.doc: Include stores a column in the index without indexing it.

IndexBuilder.Name.doc: Name sets the index name, in place of table_columns_idx.

IndexBuilder.Using.doc: Using sets the index method, such as gin.

IndexBuilder.Where.doc: Where makes the index partial, covering rows that match a SQL condition.

Interceptor.doc: Interceptor observes every statement a context runs, for logging, metrics, and tracing.

Into.doc: Into maps a column to a field of the projected type.

IntoExpr.decl: func IntoExpr[V any](dst *V, src Expr[V]) Mapping
IntoExpr.doc: IntoExpr maps an expression to a field of the projected type.

IsCheckViolation.doc: IsCheckViolation reports whether err is a check constraint failure.

IsDirty.decl: func IsDirty[T, V any](e *EntityEntry[T], field *V) bool
IsDirty.doc: IsDirty reports whether a field differs from what was loaded.

IsForeignKeyViolation.doc: IsForeignKeyViolation reports whether err is a foreign key failure.

IsNotNull.doc: IsNotNull matches rows where field is not NULL.

IsNotNullViolation.doc: IsNotNullViolation reports whether err is a NOT NULL failure.

IsNull.doc: IsNull matches rows where field is NULL.

IsRetryable.doc: IsRetryable reports whether a transaction failed from a deadlock or a serialization conflict, and would likely work if run again.

IsUniqueViolation.doc: IsUniqueViolation reports whether err is a unique constraint failure.

Isolation.doc: Isolation sets the transaction isolation level.

JSON.doc: JSON stores a Go value in a JSON column.

JSON.MarshalJSON.doc: MarshalJSON writes the value inside, so that an API response shows the document and not this wrapper.

Join2.doc: Join2 is a query across two joined models.

Join2.GroupBy.doc: GroupBy groups the joined rows by a column.

Join2.GroupByExpr.doc: GroupByExpr groups the joined rows by an expression.

Join2.Join.decl: func (j *Join2[A, B]) Join[C any](rel **C) *Join3[A, B, C]
Join2.Join.doc: Join adds a many-to-one or one-to-one relation of any model in the query.

Join2.JoinMany.decl: func (j *Join2[A, B]) JoinMany[C any](rel *[]C) *Join3[A, B, C]
Join2.JoinMany.doc: JoinMany adds a one-to-many relation of any model in the query.

Join2.JoinOn.decl: func (j *Join2[A, B]) JoinOn[C any](on ...Cond) *Join3[A, B, C]
Join2.JoinOn.doc: JoinOn adds a model on conditions.

Join2.LeftJoin.decl: func (j *Join2[A, B]) LeftJoin[C any](rel **C) *Join3[A, B, C]
Join2.LeftJoin.doc: LeftJoin adds a many-to-one or one-to-one relation, keeping unmatched rows.

Join2.LeftJoinMany.decl: func (j *Join2[A, B]) LeftJoinMany[C any](rel *[]C) *Join3[A, B, C]
Join2.LeftJoinMany.doc: LeftJoinMany adds a one-to-many relation, keeping rows with no related row.

Join2.LeftJoinOn.decl: func (j *Join2[A, B]) LeftJoinOn[C any](on ...Cond) *Join3[A, B, C]
Join2.LeftJoinOn.doc: LeftJoinOn adds a model on conditions, keeping unmatched rows.

Join2.Limit.doc: Limit caps the number of rows returned.

Join2.Order.doc: Order orders results by terms from Asc and Desc, replacing any earlier ordering.

Join2.OrderBy.doc: OrderBy orders results by a field of any joined model, ascending, replacing any earlier ordering.

Join2.OrderByDesc.doc: OrderByDesc orders results by a field of any joined model, descending, replacing any earlier ordering.

Join2.Select.decl: func (j *Join2[A, B]) Select[R any](f func(*A, *B) R) *Projection[R]
Join2.Select.doc: Select projects each joined row through f.

Join2.Where.doc: Where adds conditions on any joined model.

Join3.doc: Join3 is a query across three joined models.

Join3.Distinct.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) Distinct() *Join3[A, B, C]

Join3.GroupBy.doc: GroupBy groups the joined rows by a column.

Join3.GroupByExpr.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) GroupByExpr[V any](e Expr[V]) *Grouped
Join3.GroupByExpr.doc: GroupByExpr groups the joined rows by an expression.

Join3.Join.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) Join[D any](rel **D) *Join4[A, B, C, D]
Join3.Join.doc: Join adds a many-to-one or one-to-one relation of any model in the query.

Join3.JoinMany.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) JoinMany[D any](rel *[]D) *Join4[A, B, C, D]
Join3.JoinMany.doc: JoinMany adds a one-to-many relation of any model in the query.

Join3.JoinOn.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) JoinOn[D any](on ...Cond) *Join4[A, B, C, D]
Join3.JoinOn.doc: JoinOn adds a model on conditions.

Join3.LeftJoin.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) LeftJoin[D any](rel **D) *Join4[A, B, C, D]
Join3.LeftJoin.doc: LeftJoin adds a many-to-one or one-to-one relation, keeping unmatched rows.

Join3.LeftJoinMany.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) LeftJoinMany[D any](rel *[]D) *Join4[A, B, C, D]
Join3.LeftJoinMany.doc: LeftJoinMany adds a one-to-many relation, keeping rows with no related row.

Join3.LeftJoinOn.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) LeftJoinOn[D any](on ...Cond) *Join4[A, B, C, D]
Join3.LeftJoinOn.doc: LeftJoinOn adds a model on conditions, keeping unmatched rows.

Join3.Limit.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) Limit(limit int) *Join3[A, B, C]
Join3.Limit.doc: Limit caps the number of rows returned.

Join3.Offset.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) Offset(offset int) *Join3[A, B, C]

Join3.Order.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) Order(terms ...Sort) *Join3[A, B, C]
Join3.Order.doc: Order orders results by terms from Asc and Desc, replacing any earlier ordering.

Join3.OrderBy.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) OrderBy[V Ordered](field *V) *Join3[A, B, C]
Join3.OrderBy.doc: OrderBy orders results by a field of any joined model, ascending, replacing any earlier ordering.

Join3.OrderByDesc.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) OrderByDesc[V Ordered](field *V) *Join3[A, B, C]
Join3.OrderByDesc.doc: OrderByDesc orders results by a field of any joined model, descending, replacing any earlier ordering.

Join3.Select.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) Select[R any](f func(*A, *B, *C) R) *Projection[R]
Join3.Select.doc: Select projects each joined row through f.

Join3.Where.decl: func (j *Join3[A, B, C]) Where(c ...Cond) *Join3[A, B, C]
Join3.Where.doc: Where adds conditions on any joined model.

Join4.doc: Join4 is a query across four joined models.

Join4.Distinct.decl: func (j *Join4[A, B, C, D]) Distinct() *Join4[A, B, C, D]

Join4.GroupBy.decl: func (j *Join4[A, B, C, D]) GroupBy[V any](field *V) *Grouped
Join4.GroupBy.doc: GroupBy groups the joined rows by a column.

Join4.GroupByExpr.doc: GroupByExpr groups the joined rows by an expression.

Join4.Limit.decl: func (j *Join4[A, B, C, D]) Limit(limit int) *Join4[A, B, C, D]
Join4.Limit.doc: Limit caps the number of rows returned.

Join4.Offset.decl: func (j *Join4[A, B, C, D]) Offset(offset int) *Join4[A, B, C, D]

Join4.Order.decl: func (j *Join4[A, B, C, D]) Order(terms ...Sort) *Join4[A, B, C, D]
Join4.Order.doc: Order orders results by terms from Asc and Desc, replacing any earlier ordering.

Join4.OrderBy.decl: func (j *Join4[A, B, C, D]) OrderBy[V Ordered](field *V) *Join4[A, B, C, D]
Join4.OrderBy.doc: OrderBy orders results by a field of any joined model, ascending, replacing any earlier ordering.

Join4.OrderByDesc.decl: func (j *Join4[A, B, C, D]) OrderByDesc[V Ordered](field *V) *Join4[A, B, C, D]
Join4.OrderByDesc.doc: OrderByDesc orders results by a field of any joined model, descending, replacing any earlier ordering.

Join4.Select.decl: func (j *Join4[A, B, C, D]) Select[R any](f func(*A, *B, *C, *D) R) *Projection[R]
Join4.Select.doc: Select projects each joined row through f.

Join4.Where.decl: func (j *Join4[A, B, C, D]) Where(c ...Cond) *Join4[A, B, C, D]
Join4.Where.doc: Where adds conditions on any joined model.

JoinLateral.decl: func JoinLateral[T, J any](q *Query[T], sub *Query[J], on ...Cond) *Join2[T, J]
JoinLateral.doc: JoinLateral joins a query that runs once per row of T, so its conditions can refer to T's columns.

JoinSub.decl: func JoinSub[T, J any](q *Query[T], sub *Query[J], on ...Cond) *Join2[T, J]
JoinSub.doc: JoinSub joins the results of another query.

KeyBuilder.NotGenerated.doc: NotGenerated means the application always supplies the key, so a zero key is written as zero.

Lag.doc: Lag returns field from the previous row of a window.

Lead.doc: Lead returns field from the next row of a window.

LeftJoinLateral.decl: func LeftJoinLateral[T, J any](q *Query[T], sub *Query[J], on ...Cond) *Join2[T, J]
LeftJoinLateral.doc: LeftJoinLateral is JoinLateral, keeping rows of T with no match.

LeftJoinSub.decl: func LeftJoinSub[T, J any](q *Query[T], sub *Query[J], on ...Cond) *Join2[T, J]
LeftJoinSub.doc: LeftJoinSub is JoinSub, keeping rows of T with no match.

Length.doc: Length returns the length of a text column, in characters.

Like.doc: Like matches rows where field matches a SQL LIKE pattern, in which % matches any text and _ matches one character.

Link.decl: func Link[T, R any](ctx context.Context, h Handle, owner *T, rel *[]R, targets ...*R) error
Link.doc: Link adds rows to a many-to-many relation's join table, skipping pairs that are already there.

LogValues.doc: LogValues includes argument values in logs.

Lt.decl: func Lt[V Ordered](field *V, v V) Cond
Lt.doc: Lt matches rows where field is less than v.

Lte.decl: func Lte[V Ordered](field *V, v V) Cond
Lte.doc: Lte matches rows where field is less than or equal to v.

Mapping.doc: Mapping sets one field of a projection, from Into or IntoExpr.

MarkModified.decl: func MarkModified[T any](h Handle, entity *T) error
MarkModified.doc: MarkModified makes the next SaveChanges write every field of an entity.

Max.doc: Max returns a column's largest value.

MaxOf.decl: func MaxOf[T any, V Ordered](ctx context.Context, q *Query[T], field *V) (V, error)
MaxOf.doc: MaxOf returns a column's largest value, or zero if there are no rows.

MaxRelated.decl: func MaxRelated[R any, V Ordered](rel *[]R, field *V, conds ...Cond) Expr[sql.Null[V]]
MaxRelated.doc: MaxRelated returns the largest value of a field of the related rows.

Merge.decl: func Merge[T, S any](t *Table[T], source *Query[S], on ...Cond) *Merger[T]
Merge.doc: Merge combines source rows into T's table, deciding per row what to do, which Upsert cannot: one statement can update, insert, and delete.

Merger.Delete.doc: Delete turns the last clause, which must have no assignments, into a delete.

Merger.Exec.doc: Exec runs the statement and returns the number of rows changed.

Merger.WhenMatched.doc: WhenMatched updates target rows that have a source row.

Merger.WhenMatchedIf.doc: WhenMatchedIf updates matched rows that also meet a condition.

Merger.WhenNotMatched.doc: WhenNotMatched inserts source rows with no target row.

Min.doc: Min returns a column's smallest value.

MinOf.decl: func MinOf[T any, V Ordered](ctx context.Context, q *Query[T], field *V) (V, error)
MinOf.doc: MinOf returns a column's smallest value, or zero if there are no rows.

MinRelated.decl: func MinRelated[R any, V Ordered](rel *[]R, field *V, conds ...Cond) Expr[sql.Null[V]]
MinRelated.doc: MinRelated returns the smallest value of a field of the related rows.

Mixin.doc: Mixin configures whichever model embeds a MixinConfigurer.

Mixin.Eq.decl: func (m *Mixin) Eq(column string, value any) Cond
Mixin.Eq.doc: Eq is a condition on a column by name, for use in a Filter.

Mixin.Filter.decl: func (m *Mixin) Filter(name string, filter func(context.Context) Cond)
Mixin.Filter.doc: Filter adds a global filter, as ModelBuilder.Filter does.

Mixin.Index.doc: Index adds an index on columns of the model, named after them.

Mixin.Table.doc: Table returns the model's table name.

MixinConfigurer.doc: MixinConfigurer is implemented by a struct meant to be embedded in many models, to add the configuration that goes with its fields.

ModelBuilder.doc: ModelBuilder collects configuration for model E. Errors surface from Open.

ModelBuilder.Column.doc: Column configures how a column is declared in migrations.

ModelBuilder.Comment.doc: Comment describes the table in the database.

ModelBuilder.Comparer.decl: func (b *ModelBuilder[E]) Comparer[V any](field *V, equal func(a, b V) bool)
ModelBuilder.Comparer.doc: Comparer sets how change tracking compares a field, in place of a deep comparison.

ModelBuilder.CompositeKey.doc: CompositeKey sets a primary key of several columns.

ModelBuilder.Discriminator.doc: Discriminator shares a table between several models: rows of this one hold value in field.

ModelBuilder.ExcludeFromMigrations.doc: ExcludeFromMigrations means migrations leave this model's table alone, because something else owns it.

ModelBuilder.Filter.decl: func (b *ModelBuilder[E]) Filter(name string, filter func(context.Context) Cond)
ModelBuilder.Filter.doc: Filter adds a global filter, applied to every query of this model, including joins and subqueries.

ModelBuilder.ForeignKey.doc: ForeignKey declares a foreign key on its own, for one no relation can express, such as a key of several columns.

ModelBuilder.HasManyThrough.doc: HasManyThrough configures a read-only relation that crosses a table in between: a Country has many Posts through Users.

ModelBuilder.HasOneThrough.doc: HasOneThrough is HasManyThrough for a single related row.

ModelBuilder.Index.doc: Index declares an index on field.

ModelBuilder.IndexExpr.doc: IndexExpr declares an index on a SQL expression, such as lower(email).

ModelBuilder.KeyName.doc: KeyName names the primary key constraint, in place of table_pkey.

ModelBuilder.ManyToMany.doc: ManyToMany configures a many-to-many relation through a join table, named with Through.

ModelBuilder.NoKey.doc: NoKey removes the primary key, for rows with no identity.

ModelBuilder.NoTimestamps.doc: NoTimestamps stops CreatedAt and UpdatedAt being maintained.

ModelBuilder.PartitionByHash.doc: PartitionByHash declares the table partitioned by a hash of the columns.

ModelBuilder.PartitionByList.doc: PartitionByList declares the table partitioned by lists of column values.

ModelBuilder.PartitionByRange.doc: PartitionByRange declares the table partitioned by ranges of the columns.

ModelBuilder.Validate.decl: func (b *ModelBuilder[E]) Validate[V any](field *V, rule func(V) error)
ModelBuilder.Validate.doc: Validate adds a rule for a field, checked before Insert and SaveChanges write it, as a Validate hook is.

ModelBuilder.View.doc: View maps the model to a view, which can be queried but not written.

ModelConvention.doc: ModelConvention is one model, offered to a rule from WithConvention.

ModelConvention.Name.doc: Name returns the model's type name.

ModelConvention.SetTable.doc: SetTable changes the model's table name.

ModelConvention.Table.doc: Table returns the model's table name.

Modified.doc: Modified entities are updated by the next SaveChanges.

Naming.doc: Naming replaces the conventions that turn Go names into database names.

Ne.decl: func Ne[V comparable](field *V, v V) Cond
Ne.doc: Ne matches rows where field does not equal v.

NoneOf.decl: func NoneOf[V comparable](v V, fields ...*V) Cond
NoneOf.doc: NoneOf matches rows where none of fields equals v.

Not.doc: Not matches rows where c does not match.

NotExists.doc: NotExists matches rows for which q returns nothing.

NotIn.doc: NotIn matches rows where field equals none of values.

NotInSub.decl: func NotInSub[V any](field *V, sub Sub[V]) Cond
NotInSub.doc: NotInSub matches rows where field is none of the subquery's values.

Number.doc: Number is a type that SUM and AVG accept.

Observe.decl: func Observe[T any](h Handle, o Observer[T]) error
Observe.doc: Observe registers an observer for model T, on this context and its sessions.

Observer.doc: Observer receives entities after their change is committed, so it never sees a write that rolled back.

OnConflict.doc: OnConflict names the column of the unique constraint.

OnPrimary.doc: OnPrimary sends the reads made with ctx to the primary, not a replica.

Open.doc: Open connects to a database and returns a populated context.

Option.doc: Option configures a context in Open.

Or.doc: Or matches rows where any condition matches.

Ordered.doc: Ordered is a type with a database ordering.

OrderedBy.doc: OrderedBy starts a window over all rows in the given order.

Original.decl: func Original[T, V any](e *EntityEntry[T], field *V) (V, error)
Original.doc: Original returns a field's value as it was loaded.

Outcome.doc: Outcome is what happened to a statement.

Page.doc: Page is one page of a query, with the totals needed to show paging links.

Page.HasNext.doc: HasNext reports whether another page follows this one.

Page.Pages.doc: Pages returns the number of pages.

PartitionBy.doc: PartitionBy starts a window divided by a column.

Past.doc: Past matches rows where a time column is before the database's current time.

Pluck.decl: func Pluck[T, V any](ctx context.Context, q *Query[T], field *V) ([]V, error)
Pluck.doc: Pluck returns one column of every matching row.

Pointers.doc: Pointers returns pointers to the elements of values, for passing a slice of values to Load.

PrepareBulk.decl: func PrepareBulk[T any](h Handle, entities []*T) (*BulkRows, error)
PrepareBulk.doc: PrepareBulk fills what Insert fills in Go, such as timestamps and generated keys, and returns the values to load.

Project.doc: Project selects only the mapped expressions, and scans them into R. Use it instead of Select to avoid fetching whole rows:

Projection.doc: Projection is a query that returns values of R. Results are not tracked.

Projection.All.doc: All returns every projected row, as an empty slice if there are none.

Projection.Each.doc: Each streams projected rows, stopping after the first error.

Projection.First.doc: First returns the first projected row, or ErrNotFound.

Query.doc: Query is a query for rows of T. Queries are immutable: every builder method returns a new query, so one can safely be the base of several others.

Query.After.decl: func (q *Query[T]) After(ctx context.Context, cursor string, size int) (*CursorPage[T], error)
Query.After.doc: After returns the page following cursor, which is empty for the first page.

Query.All.doc: All returns every matching row, as an empty slice if there are none.

Query.Chunk.decl: func (q *Query[T]) Chunk(ctx context.Context, size int, f func([]*T) error) error
Query.Chunk.doc: Chunk reads matching rows in groups of size, calling f with each until f returns an error or the rows run out.

Query.ChunkByKey.decl: func (q *Query[T]) ChunkByKey(ctx context.Context, size int, f func([]*T) error) error
Query.ChunkByKey.doc: ChunkByKey reads matching rows in key order, in groups of size.

Query.Column.doc: Column limits the query to the named columns, and can be repeated.

Query.Count.doc: Count returns the number of matching rows.

Query.CrossJoin.doc: CrossJoin pairs every row of T with every row of J.

Query.Debug.doc: Debug logs this query's SQL and values when it runs, at info level, through slog's default logger.

Query.Delete.doc: Delete removes every matching row and returns the number removed.

Query.DeleteReturning.doc: DeleteReturning is Delete, returning the removed rows.

Query.DeleteSQL.doc: DeleteSQL returns the statement Delete would run.

Query.DoesNotExist.doc: DoesNotExist reports whether no row matches.

Query.Each.doc: Each streams matching rows, stopping after the first error.

Query.Except.doc: Except returns the rows of q that are not in other.

Query.Exists.doc: Exists reports whether any row matches.

Query.Explain.doc: Explain returns the database's plan for this query.

Query.Find.decl: func (q *Query[T]) Find[K comparable](ctx context.Context, key K) (*T, error)
Query.Find.doc: Find returns the entity with the given primary key, within this query's conditions, or ErrNotFound.

Query.First.doc: First returns the first matching row, or ErrNotFound.

Query.ForShare.doc: ForShare locks the selected rows against changes until the transaction ends, while allowing other readers.

Query.ForUpdate.doc: ForUpdate locks the selected rows until the transaction ends.

Query.ForceDelete.doc: ForceDelete removes rows for real, even from a soft-deleted model.

Query.From.doc: From reads from sub instead of the table.

Query.FromCTE.doc: FromCTE names sub in a WITH clause, and reads from it.

Query.FullJoinOn.doc: FullJoinOn joins J on conditions, keeping unmatched rows of both.

Query.GroupBy.doc: GroupBy groups rows by a column.

Query.GroupByExpr.doc: GroupByExpr groups rows by an expression.

Query.Hint.doc: Hint adds an optimizer hint, written /*+ hint */ before the statement, in the form extensions such as pg_hint_plan read.

Query.IgnoreFilters.doc: IgnoreFilters switches off the named global filters for this query, or all of them with no names.

Query.Include.doc: Include loads a one-to-many relation in one extra query per relation, however many parents there are.

Query.IncludeJoined.doc: IncludeJoined loads a many-to-one or one-to-one relation in the same query, through a left join, instead of the extra query IncludeOne runs.

Query.IncludeOne.doc: IncludeOne loads a many-to-one or one-to-one relation in one extra query.

Query.Intersect.doc: Intersect returns the rows in both q and other.

Query.Join.doc: Join joins through a many-to-one or one-to-one relation.

Query.JoinMany.doc: JoinMany joins through a one-to-many relation, with one result per related row.

Query.JoinOn.doc: JoinOn joins J on conditions rather than a relation.

Query.JoinUsing.doc: JoinUsing joins J on a column with the same name in both tables.

Query.Latest.doc: Latest orders by a time column, newest first.

Query.LeftJoin.doc: LeftJoin joins through a many-to-one or one-to-one relation, keeping unmatched rows.

Query.LeftJoinMany.doc: LeftJoinMany joins through a one-to-many relation, keeping rows with no related row.

Query.LeftJoinOn.doc: LeftJoinOn joins J on conditions, keeping unmatched rows of T.

Query.Limit.doc: Limit caps the number of rows returned.

Query.NoTracking.doc: NoTracking returns entities the change tracker does not see, including those from Include.

Query.NoTrackingResolved.doc: NoTrackingResolved is NoTracking, except that one row is one instance in the results, as it is with tracking.

Query.NoWait.doc: NoWait makes a lock fail at once instead of waiting for another transaction.

Query.Offset.doc: Offset skips the first n rows.

Query.Oldest.doc: Oldest orders by a time column, oldest first.

Query.Omit.doc: Omit leaves a column out of the query.

Query.Order.doc: Order orders results by terms from Asc and Desc, replacing any earlier ordering.

Query.OrderBy.doc: OrderBy orders results by field, ascending, replacing any earlier ordering.

Query.OrderByDesc.doc: OrderByDesc orders results by field, descending, replacing any earlier ordering.

Query.Page.decl: func (q *Query[T]) Page(ctx context.Context, number, size int) (*Page[T], error)
Query.Page.doc: Page returns one page, counted from 1, with the total row count.

Query.Recursive.doc: Recursive extends q with rows reached by repeatedly following a one-to-many relation of the same model, such as a folder and everything under it.

Query.RecursiveOne.doc: RecursiveOne extends q with rows reached by repeatedly following a many-to-one relation of the same model, such as a folder and all its ancestors.

Query.Restore.doc: Restore undeletes matching soft-deleted rows and returns how many.

Query.RightJoinOn.doc: RightJoinOn joins J on conditions, keeping unmatched rows of J. Their T value is nil in Select.

Query.Single.doc: Single returns the only matching row.

Query.SkipLocked.doc: SkipLocked leaves out rows that another transaction has locked, which suits job queues.

Query.Tag.doc: Tag adds a comment to the SQL, so a query can be found in database logs.

Query.ThenBy.doc: ThenBy adds an ascending ordering after OrderBy.

Query.ThenByDesc.doc: ThenByDesc adds a descending ordering after OrderBy.

Query.ToSQL.doc: ToSQL returns the SELECT this query would run.

Query.ToSQLContext.doc: ToSQLContext is ToSQL with global filters resolved against ctx.

Query.Unfiltered.doc: Unfiltered allows Update and Delete to affect every row.

Query.Union.doc: Union returns the rows of q or other, without duplicates.

Query.Update.doc: Update applies assignments to every matching row and returns the number of rows changed.

Query.UpdateReturning.doc: UpdateReturning is Update, returning the changed rows.

Query.UpdateSQL.doc: UpdateSQL returns the statement Update would run, for sending it some other way, such as in a pipelined batch.

Query.When.doc: When applies f only if ok is true, for conditions decided at runtime.

Query.Where.doc: Where adds conditions, all of which must match.

Query.With.doc: With fills a field tagged ant:"computed" from an expression, such as a count of related rows.

Rank.doc: Rank ranks rows within a window, leaving gaps after ties.

Raw.decl: func Raw[T any](h Handle, query string, args ...any) *RawQuery[T]
Raw.doc: Raw prepares a raw SQL statement.

RawFile.decl: func RawFile[T any](h Handle, fsys fs.FS, name string, args ...any) *RawQuery[T]
RawFile.doc: RawFile is Raw with the statement read from a file in fsys, such as an embed.FS.

RawQuery.doc: RawQuery is a raw SQL statement.

RawQuery.All.doc: All runs the statement and returns every row, as an empty slice if there are none.

RawQuery.Exec.doc: Exec runs the statement and returns the number of rows affected.

RawQuery.First.doc: First runs the statement and returns the first row, or ErrNotFound.

Related.decl: func Related[T, R any](h Handle, entity *T, rel *[]R) *Query[R]
Related.doc: Related returns a query for the rows related to entity through a one-to-many relation.

RelatedOne.decl: func RelatedOne[T, R any](h Handle, entity *T, rel **R) *Query[R]
RelatedOne.doc: RelatedOne returns a query for the row related to entity through a many-to-one or one-to-one relation.

RelationBuilder.ConstraintName.doc: ConstraintName names the foreign key, in place of table_column_fkey.

RelationBuilder.ForeignKey.doc: ForeignKey sets the foreign key column, on either model.

RelationBuilder.Inverse.doc: Inverse fills a pointer on each loaded child back to its parent, so a Post from Include(&U.Posts) has its User without another query.

RelationBuilder.Latest.doc: Latest makes a has-one relation the newest of many, by field: Include reads that row for each parent.

RelationBuilder.Morph.doc: Morph makes the relation polymorphic: the foreign key can refer to several tables, and field says which.

RelationBuilder.NoForeignKey.doc: NoForeignKey keeps the relation in queries and leaves its foreign key out of migrations.

RelationBuilder.NoIndex.doc: NoIndex leaves out the index migrations otherwise add on the foreign key.

RelationBuilder.Oldest.doc: Oldest makes a has-one relation the oldest of many, by field.

RelationBuilder.OnDelete.doc: OnDelete sets the action when the parent is deleted.

RelationBuilder.OnUpdate.doc: OnUpdate sets the action when the parent's key changes.

RelationBuilder.PivotColumns.doc: PivotColumns names the join table's columns, for the owner and the target.

RelationBuilder.References.doc: References sets the column the foreign key points to, in place of the primary key.

RelationBuilder.Through.doc: Through names the join table of a many-to-many relation.

RelationBuilder.Touch.doc: Touch updates the parent's UpdatedAt whenever SaveChanges writes this child, as a comment makes its post look recently active.

RelationBuilder.Where.doc: Where scopes the relation: Include, Has, joins, and counts see only the target rows that meet conds.

Remove.decl: func Remove[T any](h Handle, entity *T) error
Remove.doc: Remove schedules an entity for deletion by the next SaveChanges.

Retry.doc: Retry says how to run a transaction again after a deadlock or serialization failure, which a database reports when two transactions collide and only one can win.

Retry.Attempts.doc: Attempts is the number of runs in all.

RowNumber.doc: RowNumber numbers rows within a window, from 1.

SQL.decl: func SQL[V any](text string, args ...any) Expr[V]
SQL.doc: SQL returns an expression from raw SQL.

SQLCond.doc: SQLCond returns a condition from raw SQL.

SQLState.doc: SQLState returns the database's error code for err, or "".

SaveInterceptor.doc: SaveInterceptor is an Interceptor that also sees each SaveChanges before it writes, for auditing.

SchemaOf.doc: SchemaOf returns the schema DB's models describe: its Table fields, and models reached through their relations.

Selectable.doc: Selectable is a query that Project can read from.

Session.doc: Session returns a new context on the same connections with its own tracker, which suits one unit of work, such as one web request.

Set.decl: func Set[V any](field *V, v V) Assignment

SetExpr.decl: func SetExpr[V any](field *V, value Expr[V]) Assignment
SetExpr.doc: SetExpr assigns an expression to field, such as another column.

SlowThreshold.doc: SlowThreshold logs statements at or over d at warning level.

Sort.doc: Sort is one term of an ordering, from Asc or Desc.

Sort.NullsFirst.doc: NullsFirst sorts NULL values before all others.

Sort.NullsLast.doc: NullsLast sorts NULL values after all others.

StartAt.doc: StartAt sets a sequence's first value.

State.doc: State is the lifecycle state of an entity.

Statement.doc: Statement is one SQL statement on its way to the database.

Sub.doc: Sub is a query for one column of type V, for use in a condition or as a value.

Sub.Expr.doc: Expr uses the subquery as a single value.

SubExpr.decl: func SubExpr[V any](q Selectable, value Expr[V]) Sub[V]
SubExpr.doc: SubExpr makes q a subquery selecting an expression.

SubOf.decl: func SubOf[V any](q Selectable, field *V) Sub[V]
SubOf.doc: SubOf makes q a subquery selecting field.

SumOf.decl: func SumOf[T any, V Number](ctx context.Context, q *Query[T], field *V) (V, error)
SumOf.doc: SumOf adds up a column over matching rows, giving zero if there are none.

SumRelated.decl: func SumRelated[R any, V Number](rel *[]R, field *V, conds ...Cond) Expr[V]
SumRelated.doc: SumRelated adds up a field of the related rows, giving zero if there are none.

SyncLinks.decl: func SyncLinks[T, R any](ctx context.Context, h Handle, owner *T, rel *[]R, targets ...*R) error
SyncLinks.doc: SyncLinks makes targets the only links of owner in a many-to-many relation.

Table.doc: Table is a typed entry point to one model.

Table.Column.doc: Column starts a query limited to the named column.

Table.Count.doc: Count returns the number of rows.

Table.CrossJoin.doc: CrossJoin starts a query that pairs every row with every row of J.

Table.DeleteByID.decl: func (t *Table[T]) DeleteByID[K comparable](ctx context.Context, key K) error
Table.DeleteByID.doc: DeleteByID removes the entity with the given primary key, and stops tracking it, or returns ErrNotFound.

Table.Distinct.doc: Distinct starts a query that removes duplicate rows.

Table.Exists.doc: Exists reports whether the table has any rows.

Table.Find.decl: func (t *Table[T]) Find[K comparable](ctx context.Context, key K) (*T, error)
Table.Find.doc: Find returns the entity with the given primary key, or ErrNotFound.

Table.FindKey.doc: FindKey returns the entity with a composite primary key, given its parts in key order, or ErrNotFound.

Table.First.doc: First returns the first row, or ErrNotFound.

Table.FirstOrCreate.decl: func (t *Table[T]) FirstOrCreate(ctx context.Context, e *T, conds ...Cond) (*T, bool, error)
Table.FirstOrCreate.doc: FirstOrCreate returns the first row that meets conds, or inserts e and returns it.

Table.FirstOrNew.decl: func (t *Table[T]) FirstOrNew(ctx context.Context, e *T, conds ...Cond) (*T, bool, error)
Table.FirstOrNew.doc: FirstOrNew returns the first row that meets conds, or e, not saved.

Table.FullJoinOn.doc: FullJoinOn starts a query fully joined on conditions.

Table.GroupBy.doc: GroupBy starts a query grouped by a column.

Table.GroupByExpr.doc: GroupByExpr starts a query grouped by an expression.

Table.IgnoreFilters.doc: IgnoreFilters starts a query with the named global filters off.

Table.Include.doc: Include starts a query that loads a one-to-many relation.

Table.IncludeJoined.doc: IncludeJoined starts a query that reads a relation in the same statement.

Table.IncludeOne.doc: IncludeOne starts a query that loads a many-to-one or one-to-one relation.

Table.Insert.doc: Insert writes entities and the new entities related to them, parents first, in one transaction, so either all are saved or none are.

Table.InsertFrom.doc: InsertFrom inserts the rows of a projection, and returns how many.

Table.InsertMany.doc: InsertMany writes many rows quickly, in multi-row statements inside one transaction, and returns how many were inserted.

Table.InsertOnly.doc: InsertOnly writes entities and ignores their relation fields.

Table.Join.doc: Join starts a query joined through a relation.

Table.JoinMany.doc: JoinMany starts a query joined through a one-to-many relation.

Table.JoinOn.doc: JoinOn starts a query joined on conditions.

Table.LeftJoin.doc: LeftJoin starts a query left-joined through a relation.

Table.LeftJoinMany.doc: LeftJoinMany starts a query left-joined through a one-to-many relation.

Table.LeftJoinOn.doc: LeftJoinOn starts a query left-joined on conditions.

Table.Limit.doc: Limit starts a query capped at n rows.

Table.Load.decl: func (t *Table[T]) Load[R any](ctx context.Context, rel *[]R, entities ...*T) error
Table.Load.doc: Load fills a one-to-many relation on entities already in memory, in one extra query.

Table.LoadMissing.decl: func (t *Table[T]) LoadMissing[R any](ctx context.Context, rel *[]R, entities ...*T) error
Table.LoadMissing.doc: LoadMissing is Load for only the entities whose relation is still nil.

Table.LoadOne.decl: func (t *Table[T]) LoadOne[R any](ctx context.Context, rel **R, entities ...*T) error
Table.LoadOne.doc: LoadOne fills a many-to-one or one-to-one relation on entities already in memory, in one extra query.

Table.NoTracking.doc: NoTracking starts a query whose results are not tracked.

Table.Offset.doc: Offset starts a query that skips n rows.

Table.Omit.doc: Omit starts a query that leaves a column out.

Table.OnlyDeleted.doc: OnlyDeleted starts a query for soft-deleted rows.

Table.Order.doc: Order starts a query ordered by terms from Asc and Desc.

Table.OrderBy.doc: OrderBy starts a query ordered by field, ascending.

Table.OrderByDesc.doc: OrderByDesc starts a query ordered by field, descending.

Table.Prune.doc: Prune removes rows that meet conds for good, soft-deleted or not, in batches, so that clearing out old rows does not hold one long transaction.

Table.Query.doc: Query starts a query with nothing added yet.

Table.Reload.doc: Reload overwrites the columns of e with the stored row, found by e's primary key, or returns ErrNotFound.

Table.RightJoinOn.doc: RightJoinOn starts a query right-joined on conditions.

Table.Scope.doc: Scope starts a query from reusable logic.

Table.Truncate.doc: Truncate removes every row, faster than Delete, and cannot be used on a table that others refer to unless they are empty too.

Table.Unfiltered.doc: Unfiltered starts a query whose Update or Delete affects every row.

Table.UpdateMany.doc: UpdateMany writes the named columns of each entity to its own row, in one transaction, and returns how many rows changed.

Table.Upsert.decl: func (t *Table[T]) Upsert(ctx context.Context, e *T, conflict *Conflict) (bool, error)
Table.Upsert.doc: Upsert inserts e, or follows conflict if a unique constraint already holds the row.

Table.Where.doc: Where starts a query with conditions.

Table.With.doc: With starts a query that fills a computed field.

Table.WithDeleted.doc: WithDeleted starts a query that includes soft-deleted rows.

TableOf.decl: func TableOf[T any]() (schemaName, table string, err error)
TableOf.doc: TableOf returns the database schema and table of model T, as configured.

Then.doc: Then groups by another column as well.

Today.doc: Today matches rows where a time column falls on the database's current date.

Toggle.decl: func Toggle[T, R any](ctx context.Context, h Handle, owner *T, rel *[]R, targets ...*R) error
Toggle.doc: Toggle links the targets that are not linked to owner, and unlinks those that are.

TrackGraph.decl: func TrackGraph[T any](h Handle, root *T, decide func(GraphNode) State) error
TrackGraph.doc: TrackGraph walks a graph that came from outside, such as a request body, and tracks each entity in the state decide returns for it.

Tracked.doc: Tracked returns the tracked entities of type T, oldest first.

Unchanged.doc: Unchanged entities match what was loaded.

UnixTime.doc: UnixTime is a time stored as whole seconds since 1970.

Unlink.decl: func Unlink[T, R any](ctx context.Context, h Handle, owner *T, rel *[]R, targets ...*R) error
Unlink.doc: Unlink removes rows from a many-to-many relation's join table.

UseConn.doc: UseConn returns a context on one connection from database/sql, such as one holding a session setting or an advisory lock.

UseTx.doc: UseTx returns a context bound to a transaction started outside ant, so that ant's queries can join it.

ValidationError.doc: ValidationError reports a field that failed a rule from ModelBuilder.Validate.

Validator.doc: Validator checks an entity before Insert or SaveChanges writes it.

Values.doc: Values reads rows held in memory as if they were a table, for joining against a list or using it in a subquery.

Watch.doc: Watch returns a context that counts statements for Diagnostics.

Window.doc: Window is an OVER clause, from PartitionBy or OrderedBy.

Window.OrderBy.doc: OrderBy orders rows within the window.

Window.PartitionBy.doc: PartitionBy divides the window by more expressions.

WithConflict.doc: WithConflict applies a Conflict to every row of InsertMany.

WithConvention.doc: WithConvention adds a rule applied to every model as it is configured, before its Configure method, which can override it.

WithDetailedErrors.doc: WithDetailedErrors adds the failing statement to every query error's message, which helps in development.

WithEvents.doc: WithEvents registers callbacks on the context and its sessions.

WithLogger.doc: WithLogger logs every statement to logger: failures at error level, slow ones at warning level, and the rest at debug level.

WithLooseScan.doc: WithLooseScan ignores result columns with no field.

WithNaming.doc: WithNaming sets a naming strategy, such as PascalCase table names for an existing database.

WithNow.doc: WithNow sets the clock for automatic timestamps, which suits tests.

WithReplicas.doc: WithReplicas sends reads outside transactions to these pools in turn.

WithRetry.doc: WithRetry applies a retry policy to every Tx and SaveChanges of this context, unless Attempts says otherwise for one call.

WithStickyWrites.doc: WithStickyWrites sends a context's reads to the primary for d after each of its writes, so that replication lag cannot hide what it just wrote.

WithStrict.doc: WithStrict makes a query fail if a result column has no field, which usually means a model has fallen behind the schema, or a SELECT * picked up something new.

WithTracking.doc: WithTracking sets whether queries track what they load.

WithoutAutoTx.doc: WithoutAutoTx stops SaveChanges and Insert from opening a transaction of their own, so a failure partway leaves earlier statements in place.

WithoutHooks.doc: WithoutHooks skips model hooks for writes made with ctx.

Wrap.decl: func Wrap[DB any](d dialect.Dialect, pool *sql.DB, options ...Option) (*DB, error)
Wrap.doc: Wrap returns a context on an existing pool.

Factory.doc: Factory makes valid entities for tests, so a test states only what it cares about.

Factory.AfterBuild.doc: AfterBuild returns a factory that calls fn on each entity it builds.

Factory.AfterCreate.doc: AfterCreate returns a factory that calls fn on each entity it inserts, with its generated key in place, which is the place to add related rows.

Factory.Build.doc: Build returns an entity without touching a database.

Factory.Create.doc: Create builds an entity and inserts it, and its related entities, through table.

Factory.With.doc: With returns a factory that applies overrides, as a named state or a one-off.

Isolate.doc: Isolate returns a context bound to a transaction that rolls back when t ends, so a test leaves nothing behind and tests can share a database.

Load.decl: func Load[DB any](t testing.TB, db *DB, fsys fs.FS, files ...string)
Load.doc: Load inserts rows from JSON files.

Recycle.doc: Recycle returns a shared parent made by f.

Recycled.doc: Recycled shares one parent among many children, so a hundred posts do not create a hundred authors.

Bind.decl: func Bind(d Dialect, query string, args []any) (string, []any, error)
Bind.doc: Bind prepares raw SQL for d.

ConflictWhere.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

DateCast.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

DatePart.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

DefaultKeyword.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

Dialect.doc: Dialect adapts ant to one database.

Dialect.DriverName.doc: DriverName is the database/sql driver to open.

Dialect.Name.doc: Name identifies the dialect, such as "postgres".

Dialect.Placeholder.doc: Placeholder returns the bind parameter for position n, counted from 1.

Dialect.Render.decl: Render(stmt qb.Statement) (sql string, args []any, err error)
Dialect.Render.doc: Render converts a statement to SQL and its arguments.

Dialect.SupportsReturning.doc: SupportsReturning reports whether an INSERT can hand back columns, through RETURNING or an equivalent.

Feature.doc: Feature names something that not every database has.

FullJoin.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

LateralJoin.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

Merge.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

Numbered.decl: func Numbered(prefix string, n int) string
Numbered.doc: Numbered returns a numbered placeholder, such as "$1" or "@p1".

OnConflict.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

QuoteWith.decl: func QuoteWith(ident, open, close string) string
QuoteWith.doc: QuoteWith wraps ident in open and close, doubling any embedded close.

RegisterErrors.doc: RegisterErrors adds a function that turns a driver's error into a SQLSTATE code, or "", for a database whose driver does not report one.

Render.decl: func Render(d Dialect, stmt qb.Statement) (string, []any, error)
Render.doc: Render converts a statement to SQL using d's placeholders and quoting.

ReturningDelete.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

ReturningInsert.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

ReturningUpdate.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

RowLocks.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

ShareLocks.doc: The features a dialect can lack.

StateOf.doc: StateOf returns the SQLSTATE code a registered dialect finds in err, or "".

Supports.decl: func Supports(d Dialect, f Feature) bool
Supports.doc: Supports reports whether d's database has f.

Syntactic.doc: Syntactic is implemented by a dialect whose SQL differs from PostgreSQL's.

Syntax.doc: Syntax says where a dialect's SQL differs from what Render writes, which is PostgreSQL's.

Syntax.BareSets.doc: BareSets leaves the parentheses off UNION members.

Syntax.DuplicateKey.doc: DuplicateKey writes ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE in place of ON CONFLICT.

Syntax.EmptyValues.doc: EmptyValues writes VALUES () in place of DEFAULT VALUES.

Syntax.Functions.doc: Functions renames functions, such as LENGTH to LEN.

Syntax.HintInSelect.doc: HintInSelect moves an optimizer hint to just after SELECT.

Syntax.Lacks.doc: Lacks reports whether the database is missing f.

Syntax.MaxParameters.doc: MaxParameters is the most bound values in one statement.

Syntax.MergeSemicolon.doc: MergeSemicolon ends MERGE with the semicolon the database demands.

Syntax.Missing.doc: Missing lists the features the database lacks.

Syntax.NoBooleans.doc: NoBooleans turns EXISTS used as a value into a CASE.

Syntax.NoFilter.doc: NoFilter turns an aggregate's FILTER into a CASE inside it.

Syntax.NoILike.doc: NoILike turns ILIKE into a LIKE between lowered values.

Syntax.NoNullsOrder.doc: NoNullsOrder turns NULLS FIRST and NULLS LAST into a CASE before the value.

Syntax.NoRowIn.doc: NoRowIn spells out multi-column IN as ORs.

Syntax.OffsetFetch.doc: OffsetFetch writes OFFSET n ROWS FETCH NEXT m ROWS ONLY for paging, which needs an ORDER BY, so one is added if the query has none.

Syntax.Output.doc: Output writes OUTPUT INSERTED.x in place of RETURNING x.

Syntax.ParameterLimit.doc: ParameterLimit returns the most bound values in one statement.

Syntax.SavepointCommands.doc: SavepointCommands returns the commands that take a savepoint's name.

Syntax.TransactSavepoints.doc: TransactSavepoints uses SAVE TRANSACTION, which has no release.

Syntax.UTCTimes.doc: UTCTimes binds times in UTC, for a database whose columns drop the zone, so that every stored time is on one clock.

Syntax.Unlimited.doc: Unlimited is the LIMIT to write when a query has only an OFFSET, for a database that cannot have one without the other.

Syntax.ValuesUnion.doc: ValuesUnion writes a VALUES source as SELECTs joined by UNION ALL, for a database that cannot name its columns.

Syntax.WrapLimitedIn.doc: WrapLimitedIn puts a derived table around a subquery with a LIMIT inside IN, for a database that refuses it directly.

NewSnowflake.doc: NewSnowflake returns a generator for a node from 0 to 1023.

Snowflake.doc: Snowflake makes 63-bit integer keys that sort by time: 41 bits of milliseconds since an epoch, 10 bits of node, and 12 bits of sequence.

ULID.doc: ULID returns a 26-character ULID: a millisecond timestamp and random bits in Crockford base 32, which sorts by time as text.

UUID.doc: UUID returns a version 7 UUID in its usual text form: a millisecond timestamp followed by random bits, so values sort by time.

Metrics.doc: Metrics is an ant.Interceptor that counts statements by kind.

Metrics.After.decl: func (m *Metrics) After(_ context.Context, s *ant.Statement, o ant.Outcome)

Metrics.ServeHTTP.doc: ServeHTTP makes Metrics an http.Handler for /metrics.

Metrics.WritePrometheus.doc: WritePrometheus writes the metrics in Prometheus text format.

Sample.doc: Sample is one kind of statement's totals.

Applied.doc: Applied describes a migration that just ran.

Config.DSN.doc: DSN connects the commands that need a database.

Config.Dir.doc: Dir is the folder holding the migration folders.

Config.Embedded.doc: Embedded is used in place of Dir when that folder is not on disk, so one program can generate migrations in a repository and apply them once deployed, where only its binary exists.

Config.FS.doc: FS reads migrations from a file system, such as a go:embed one, instead of the disk.

Config.HistoryTable.doc: HistoryTable and HistorySchema say where applied migrations are recorded.

Config.Ignore.doc: Ignore lists names for drift to overlook, as path.Match patterns: table or schema.table for a table, table.object for a column, index, or constraint.

Config.Name.doc: Name chooses a new migration's file name.

Config.NoLock.doc: NoLock turns off the migration lock, for connection poolers that break session locks.

Config.OnApply.doc: OnApply runs after each migration is applied, for logs and metrics.

Config.OutOfOrder.doc: OutOfOrder lets a pending migration run even if a newer one is applied.

Config.Parse.decl: Parse func(file string) (version, name string, ok bool)
Config.Parse.doc: Parse reads a version and name from a file name.

Config.PerDialect.doc: PerDialect keeps each dialect's migrations in Dir/<dialect>, for a project that runs on several databases.

Config.Render.doc: Render replaces how a plan becomes SQL.

Config.SeedHooks.doc: SeedHooks runs model hooks while seeding.

Config.Skip.doc: Skip lists versions to leave unapplied, for a migration that must not run in some environment.

Config.VersionsDir.doc: VersionsDir and CodeDir name the two folders inside Dir.

DefaultName.doc: DefaultName is the default file name: 0003_add_bio.up.sql.

Dir.doc: Dir returns a Store over a folder on disk that holds versions and code folders.

Entry.doc: Entry is the status of one migration.

ErrBadMigration.doc: ErrBadMigration reports a migration that cannot be used as it is.

ErrBehindSquash.decl: var ErrBehindSquash = errors.New("ant: database is behind a squashed baseline")
ErrBehindSquash.doc: ErrBehindSquash reports a database too old for a squashed baseline.

ErrChecksum.decl: var ErrChecksum = errors.New("ant: applied migration was changed")
ErrChecksum.doc: ErrChecksum reports an applied migration whose file has changed.

ErrDrift.decl: var ErrDrift = errors.New("ant: database differs from the migrations")
ErrDrift.doc: ErrDrift reports a database that differs from what migrations describe.

ErrDuplicateVersion.decl: var ErrDuplicateVersion = errors.New("ant: two migrations share a version")
ErrDuplicateVersion.doc: ErrDuplicateVersion reports two migrations with one version, which usually comes from merging two branches.

ErrFailed.decl: var ErrFailed = errors.New("ant: a migration failed partway")
ErrFailed.doc: ErrFailed reports a migration that failed partway outside a transaction, so the database needs a look.

ErrMissing.decl: var ErrMissing = errors.New("ant: applied migration is missing")
ErrMissing.doc: ErrMissing reports an applied migration with no file.

ErrOutOfOrder.decl: var ErrOutOfOrder = errors.New("ant: pending migration is older than an applied one")
ErrOutOfOrder.doc: ErrOutOfOrder reports a pending migration older than one already applied, which usually comes from merging two branches.

ErrPending.decl: var ErrPending = errors.New("ant: migrations are pending")
ErrPending.doc: ErrPending reports migrations that have not been applied.

ErrPendingChanges.decl: var ErrPendingChanges = errors.New("ant: models have changes with no migration")
ErrPendingChanges.doc: ErrPendingChanges reports models that differ from the snapshot.

ErrReadOnly.decl: var ErrReadOnly = errors.New("ant: migration source cannot be written")
ErrReadOnly.doc: ErrReadOnly reports a command that writes, on a Source that cannot.

ErrStaleSnapshot.decl: var ErrStaleSnapshot = errors.New("ant: snapshot does not match the migration files")
ErrStaleSnapshot.doc: ErrStaleSnapshot reports a snapshot that is out of step with the migration files.

ErrUnconfirmed.doc: ErrUnconfirmed reports a destructive command that was not confirmed.

FS.doc: FS returns a read-only Source over a file system, such as an embed.FS, that holds versions and code folders at its root.

Kind.doc: Kind says how a migration runs.

Migration.doc: Migration is one unit of schema change.

Migration.Checksum.doc: Checksum identifies the migration's contents, whatever the line endings, so a checkout on Windows does not look like an edit.

Migration.File.doc: File is where the migration lives, relative to its folder.

Migration.ID.doc: ID identifies the migration in messages and in the snapshot.

Migration.Name.doc: Name is the descriptive part, such as add_bio.

Next.doc: Next describes the migration about to be named.

Next.Name.doc: the name given to the command, cleaned up

NoTransaction.doc: NoTransaction runs a Go migration outside a transaction, for work on large tables that commits in batches.

Register.decl: func Register[DB any](id string, fn func(ctx context.Context, tx *DB) error, options ...GoOption)
Register.doc: Register adds a data migration written in Go, for changes SQL cannot express.

Repeatable.doc: Repeatable migrations run after the versioned ones, and again whenever they change.

Run.decl: func Run[DB any](ctx context.Context, d dialect.Dialect, args []string, config ...Config) error
Run.doc: Run is Main without the exit, for embedding the commands in a larger program.

Seed.decl: func Seed[DB any](name string, fn Seeder[DB])
Seed.doc: Seed adds a seeder, run in registration order by the seed command, each in its own transaction.

Seeder.decl: type Seeder[] func(ctx context.Context, db *DB) error
Seeder.doc: Seeder fills a database with data.

Source.doc: Source is where migrations come from.

Source.List.doc: List returns every migration, in any order.

Source.Snapshot.doc: Snapshot returns the stored schema snapshot, or nil if there is none.

State.doc: State says where a migration stands.

Status.decl: func Status[DB any](ctx context.Context, db *DB, config ...Config) ([]Entry, error)
Status.doc: Status returns every migration and where it stands, without changing anything.

Store.doc: Store is a Source that can also be written, which generating commands need.

Store.Remove.doc: Remove deletes a migration, when squashing.

Timestamped.doc: Timestamped names files by time, as in 20261031120501_add_bio.up.sql, which avoids most version clashes between branches.

Up.decl: func Up[DB any](ctx context.Context, db *DB, config ...Config) error
Up.doc: Up applies pending migrations, then repeatable ones that are new or changed.

Versioned.doc: Versioned migrations run once, in order.

Dialect.doc: Dialect is the MySQL dialect, for version 8.0 or later.

MariaDB.doc: MariaDB is the MariaDB dialect, for version 10.5 or later, which adds INSERT and DELETE ...

New.doc: New returns an interceptor for tracer.

Tracer.doc: Tracer is an ant.Interceptor that starts a span per statement.

Batch.doc: Batch queues statements to send in one round trip, which pays off when a network sits between the application and the database.

Batch.Add.decl: func (b *Batch) Add(query string, args []any, err error) *Batch
Batch.Add.doc: Add queues a statement from a function that returns one, such as UpdateSQL.

Batch.Len.doc: Len returns the number of queued statements.

Batch.Send.decl: func (b *Batch) Send(ctx context.Context, h Database) ([]int64, error)
Batch.Send.doc: Send runs the queued statements and returns the rows each affected.

Copy.decl: func Copy[T any](ctx context.Context, h Database, entities []*T) (int64, error)
Copy.doc: Copy loads entities with COPY, which is by far the fastest way to insert many rows.

Database.doc: Database is a context that embeds ant.Context.

ErrNotPgx.decl: var ErrNotPgx = errors.New("ant: pgxext needs the pgx stdlib driver")
ErrNotPgx.doc: ErrNotPgx reports a connection from some other driver.

Array.doc: Array stores a slice in a PostgreSQL array column of text, numbers, or booleans.

Array.Value.doc: Value implements driver.Valuer, in PostgreSQL's array text format.

CosineDistance.doc: CosineDistance returns the distance from a vector column to v, for ordering by similarity: Order(postgres.CosineDistance(&D.Embedding, query).Asc()).Limit(10).

Database.doc: Database is a context that embeds ant.Context.

Distance.doc: Distance returns how far a point column is from p, in the column's units.

JSONContains.decl: func JSONContains[V any](field *V, value any) ant.Cond
JSONContains.doc: JSONContains matches rows whose jsonb column contains value.

JSONHasKey.decl: func JSONHasKey[V any](field *V, key string) ant.Cond
JSONHasKey.doc: JSONHasKey matches rows whose jsonb column has key at the top level.

JSONLength.doc: JSONLength returns the number of elements in a jsonb array column.

JSONSet.decl: func JSONSet[V any](field *V, value any, path ...string) ant.Expr[V]
JSONSet.doc: JSONSet returns a jsonb column with the value at path replaced, or added if the path's parent exists, for updating part of a document in one statement:

JSONText.doc: JSONText reads a value inside a JSON column as text, following path.

L2Distance.doc: L2Distance returns the Euclidean distance from a vector column to v.

Match.decl: func Match[V ~string](field *V, config, query string) ant.Cond
Match.doc: Match matches rows whose text column meets a full-text search, in websearch syntax, using the given text search configuration, such as "english".

MonthlyPartitions.doc: MonthlyPartitions returns the manager for model T's table.

Near.decl: func Near(field *Point, p Point, radius float64) ant.Cond
Near.doc: Near matches rows whose point column is within radius of p.

Partition.doc: Partition is one month of a table.

Partitions.doc: Partitions manages the monthly partitions of a table declared with b.PartitionByRange on a time column.

Partitions.DropBefore.decl: func (p *Partitions) DropBefore(ctx context.Context, cutoff time.Time) ([]string, error)
Partitions.DropBefore.doc: DropBefore removes every partition whose whole month ended at or before cutoff, with its rows, and returns their names.

Partitions.Ensure.doc: Ensure creates the partitions for the month holding from and the months after it, and returns the ones it created.

Partitions.List.doc: List returns the monthly partitions, oldest first.

Point.doc: Point is a location in PostgreSQL's built-in point type, which needs no extension.

Vector.doc: Vector is a column of the pgvector extension, for similarity search.

Vector.Value.doc: Value implements driver.Valuer, in pgvector's text format.

Aliased.decl: func Aliased(c Cond, table *TableRef, alias string) Cond
Aliased.doc: Aliased returns c with columns of table qualified by alias instead.

And.doc: And is true when every child is true.

Assignment.doc: Assignment sets a column in an UPDATE.

Binary.doc: Binary is a binary operator, such as addition.

Cast.doc: Cast converts a value to a database type.

Cond.doc: Cond is a node in a condition tree.

Conflict.doc: Conflict is an ON CONFLICT clause.

Contextual.doc: Contextual carries the call's context to the renderer, for Lazy conditions.

Default.doc: Default is the DEFAULT keyword in an INSERT.

Exists.doc: Exists tests whether a subquery has rows.

Expr.doc: Expr is a value in a statement.

Fragment.Needs.doc: Needs names a capability the text depends on, so a database without it gets a clear error.

In.doc: In tests membership in a list, or in a subquery if Sub is set.

JoinKind.doc: JoinKind is the type of a join.

Lazy.doc: Lazy is a condition built at render time, when the call's context is known.

MatchesAll.doc: MatchesAll reports whether c is true for every row regardless of the data, such as an And with no children or a NotIn with no values.

MergeAction.doc: MergeAction is one WHEN clause of a Merge.

NullsOrder.doc: NullsOrder places NULLs in an ordering.

Or.doc: Or is true when any child is true.

Order.doc: Order is one ORDER BY term.

Row.doc: Row is a parenthesized list of values, as in (a, b) IN ((1, 2)).

Secret.doc: Secret holds a value that must stay out of logs.

Select.Hint.doc: an optimizer hint, written /*+ like this */

Selected.doc: Selected is one item of a SELECT list.

SetOp.doc: SetOp is a UNION, INTERSECT, or EXCEPT arm.

Source.doc: Source is a table, subquery, name, or raw SQL in a FROM or JOIN.

Source.Name.doc: a CTE or other unqualified name

Statement.doc: Statement is a complete statement a dialect can render.

Values.doc: Values is a VALUES list used as a table.

When.doc: When is one branch of a Case.

AddEnumValue.doc: AddEnumValue adds a value to an enum.

AlterColumn.doc: AlterColumn changes a column from one definition to another.

Backfill.doc: Backfill fills AddColumn.Backfill on changes that need it, with the dialect's zero value.
